company.name: Lob
company.shortDescription: Lob provides direct mail and address verification APIs which allows businesses to send personalized mail to their customers.
company.description:
Lob automates direct mail for modern businesses. More than 7,000 companies use Lob’s APIs to move faster and create new growth opportunities. Lob’s APIs dramatically reduce mail processing time, reclaiming thousands of hours and improving data quality. One in four households in the U.S. have received mail generated through Lob’s platform. 

Headquartered in San Francisco, Lob is backed by leading investors including Y Combinator, First Round Capital and Polaris Partners.

productsAndServices.description: An API that automates the creation, customization, and sending of physical mail such as postcards, letters, and checks directly from software platforms.

productsAndServices.description: An API that verifies, standardizes, and enriches addresses in real time or in bulk to reduce mail delivery errors and improve data quality.

productsAndServices.description: A tool for targeting and reaching specific audiences with direct mail using demographic, geographic, and behavioral data.

insights.title: Funding is concentrated in the latest major round
insights.statement: The latest disclosed Series C round raised $50,000,000, or 60.78% of reported total funding.
insights.implication: This round accounts for most reported historical financing, making it important when assessing funding-source concentration and fundraising cadence.

insights.title: Valuation increased across disclosed rounds
insights.statement: Known post-money valuation rose from $4,604,802 to $466,562,221, a 101.32x increase.
insights.implication: The disclosed financing history indicates a material valuation step-up between the earliest and latest rounds with known valuations.
caveats: Only rounds with a disclosed post-money valuation are compared.

insights.title: Sharp recent attention and growth momentum
insights.statement: Crunchbase scores growth at 72 (-13 over 90 days) and market heat at 54 (+4).
insights.implication: The company has recently become much more visible, but the scores should be treated as attention/activity indicators rather than revenue or clinical-performance metrics.
caveats: Crunchbase does not expose the complete weighting behind these proprietary scores.

insights.title: Competitive benchmark reflects the modeled peer set

insights.implication: These matches provide a starting point for comparing differentiation, scale, and shared specialties, but they should not be treated as a verified competitor set.
